note: Scripted-run cases (D04-TIM-*, D04-SRC-*, D04-CAP-*, D04-SUB-*, D04-MIX-*) come from scenarios.json, which reference.py produces. Each invariant maps to named Rust tests in crates/franken-speaker/src/render.rs and render_log.rs, which run only under central verification, so D04-RUST-CENTRAL is blocked until that run exists.

cases.needs: cargo test -p franken-speaker (the count printed by the runner), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo fmt --all -- --check, plus the two device speaker builds, each via RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec. The loop's behavior is only its Rust tests; this runner never builds.

measured render execution time on each board class against the 25% reserve, the real driver's submission lead and underrun signal (E04 has mapped neither), and a 24-hour clean-network campaign. Render cost here is injected; guest wall-clock results never substitute for board CPU measurements.

a supervisor and hardware evidence that the amplifier is muted when the render process dies. In-process, only what the dying owner leaves behind can be shown (buffers kept alive, a best-effort mute requested); whether the amplifier muted is not observable here.

the production control runtime: regions for device lifetime and streams, cancellation ownership, pre-admitted task and finalizer capacity, and the render task's separately measured budget. This loop takes its commands through a bounded ControlPort and never waits on it; binding that port to the P03 runtime is open.

invariants.text: ready, running, muted, draining, stopped and faulted: every transition is taken and every illegal one is refused with a typed error; a stale command does not outlive a stop; block-in-progress follows start and finish and clears on cancellation

what the render path cannot carry is refused before Running; the cleanup reserve is pre-admitted; logical capacity rejection is typed and distinct from memory exhaustion; injected admission failures fail closed at start and reconnect and the stop path still finishes
block k is released on the period, must be submitted by its deadline, and is presented a minimum lead later; the one CPU does one block at a time
a render ending exactly on its deadline is on time and one tick later is dropped, never submitted late
a late wake-up that still meets the deadline is on time and one that does not is a CPU miss, counted as a late wake
consecutive CPU misses trip the watchdog, which requests a mute, records whether it was acknowledged and stops rendering
ingress loss, decode delay, CPU miss and driver underrun are four separate counters; only lost content starts a new epoch; a dry device the loop already explains is not blamed on the driver
a short write is retried within the tick and the unaccepted rest is discarded and counted, never carried as old audio
a buffer the device may read is freed only by the device's acknowledgment; a stop that is not acknowledged faults and quarantines
device loss is a persistent fault whose mute cannot be acknowledged and which a reset cannot recover; process death leaves the kernel's buffers alive and claims no acknowledgment

a control storm is bounded; a blocked management request cannot hold the render owner's lock; mute and stop are never refused; mute supersedes older queued unmute requests while a newer unmute remains permitted
a protection DSP that stops being active faults the loop and requests a mute

what reaches the device is exactly what the stages produce, in order, in the stated byte order, without loss or repeat; a graceful stop ramps to silence and ends within the ramp plus the stop deadline; one-frame blocks index safely
a full or unread event sink changes no deadline and no outcome, and what it dropped is counted
the committed scripted runs, produced by the independent model, replay through the real loop block for block

a consumed counter that goes backwards (more than half the 32-bit range behind, across the wrap too) is told apart from one that ran ahead by its own HAL code, recorded after the overclaim it qualifies and never after a forward claim, with the same safety response (mute, quarantine, credit nothing); the loop faults with its own reason, invalidates the presentation mapping, holds every buffer for as long as it takes (a timeout frees nothing), stays Faulted until an acknowledged reset takes a new baseline, and then refuses to start until the owner reinstalls its mapping; a forward overclaim leaves the mapping valid; a regress during a drain, and while muted, behave the same

exactly one critical ffw.log.v1 line carries the regress reaction (cause driver_counter_regress, message ending mapping_invalidated); the faulted state line after it names none; a forward overclaim writes no such line; an independent model and the Rust reproduce the same hand-written lines
the runner's comparison is not vacuous
files, shared scenarios, generation, mapping and hygiene hold
what cannot be verified here is counted as blocked, never passed
every line the diagnostics log writes is exactly the versioned ffw.log.v1 shape, survives its redactor unchanged, and carries only enum names, numbers and validated identifiers

a line names the cause apart (ingress loss, decode delay, CPU miss, capacity rejection, short write, driver), the injected failure in force, the state revision, the source epoch and the lateness; an independent model and the Rust reproduce the same hand-written lines

the log is bounded and never blocks; a full log drops ordinary lines first and keeps a fault; a lost critical line, here or in the loop's own queue, marks the evidence incomplete; a tiny, absent or never-drained log changes nothing the loop does

not_covered: The sample path against an independent numeric model: a differential test pins that what reaches the device is what the committed D02 and D03 stages produce, block for block, but no Python model of the filter, limiter and resampler arithmetic exists here (D02 and D03 each have their own independent references).
The real driver: its submission lead, underrun signal and byte order are not mapped (E04 is all unknown), so the lead is the fake's and the byte order is a stated harness model.
Board CPU: render cost is injected, so no CPU, p99.99 or 24-hour claim is made.
The P03 control runtime and process-death mute: see D04-OPEN-P03 and D04-EXT-PROCDEATH.

The real driver's counter: the regress reaction is shown against the fake device's counter only. What a real driver does when its counter is reset (rewind to zero, a pause, a jump, a restart that keeps counting) is not mapped (E04 is all unknown), so whether the right reaction is to fault and wait for the owner, as here, or to resynchronize on its own is open. The loop does not re-derive the presentation mapping: that lives with the owner, who must say so (reinstall_presentation_mapping) before the loop will run again.
